chunks: My father narrated to him, may God be pleased with him, who said: Sa'd ibn Abdullah narrated to me, saying: Al-Hasan ibn Musa al-Khishab narrated to me, from Isma'il ibn Mihran, from Ali ibn Uthman, from Abu al-Hasan Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon them both), who said:
The Prophets, the offspring of the Prophets, and the followers of the Prophets were distinguished by three characteristics: illness in the bodies, fear of the ruler, and poverty.
ai.seo_question: What are the three unique characteristics of the Prophets and their followers?
ai.summary: Imam Musa ibn Ja'far (peace be upon him) identifies physical illness, fear of political rulers, and poverty as the three distinctive trials that purify the spiritual status of Prophets, their progeny, and their devoted followers. This narration, found in Shaykh al-Saduq’s *Al-Khisal*, underscores the Shia theological view that these hardships are not merely misfortunes but divine honors that distinguish the righteous from the worldly, reflecting the historical reality of the Ahl al-Bayt's endurance under Umayyad and Abbasid rule.

en.dr-ali-peiravi: 3-24 (The compiler of the book narrated) that his father - may God be pleased with him - narrated that Sa’ed ibn Abdullah quoted Al-Hassan ibn Musa al-Khishab, on the authority of Isma’il ibn Mihran, on the authority of Ali ibn Uthman that Abil Hassan Musa ibn Ja’far (MGB) said,
“There are three things unique to the Prophets, their offspring and their followers: physical illness, fear of the kings, and poverty.”
